blueprint_topic: Pharmacological and Parenteral Therapies — sublingual nitroglycerin/PDE-5 inhibitor contraindication
stem: A client with angina who uses sublingual nitroglycerin reports taking sildenafil. Which teaching should the nurse reinforce?

options.A: Sildenafil use makes sublingual nitroglycerin contraindicated because PDE-5 inhibition can potentiate the nitrate effect and cause severe hypotension.
options.B: Sublingual nitroglycerin can be taken with sildenafil if the client remains seated because positioning prevents the clinically important interaction.
options.C: Sublingual nitroglycerin can be taken with sildenafil at half the usual tablet dose because dose reduction prevents severe nitrate-related hypotension.
options.D: Sildenafil mainly reduces nitroglycerin effectiveness, so an additional nitroglycerin dose may be needed to obtain the expected antianginal effect.

rationale: Current nitroglycerin sublingual-tablet prescribing information lists use of PDE-5 inhibitors such as sildenafil as a contraindication. The label states that concomitant use can cause severe hypotension, syncope, or myocardial ischemia because PDE-5 inhibitors potentiate the hypotensive effects of organic nitrates. Therefore A is the best answer. B and C incorrectly imply that posture or dose reduction makes the combination acceptable. D reverses the interaction by suggesting loss of nitrate effect rather than potentiation of hypotension.
educational_objective: Recognize sildenafil and other PDE-5 inhibitors as contraindicated with sublingual nitroglycerin because concomitant use can markedly potentiate nitrate-induced hypotension and cause serious cardiovascular complications.
source_organization: DailyMed (U.S. National Library of Medicine); Solco Healthcare U.S., LLC
source_version_date: Revised April 2025; current DailyMed label accessed 2026-08-26
source_locator: Full Prescribing Information §4.1 PDE-5-Inhibitors and sGC-Stimulators: do not use nitroglycerin sublingual tablets in patients taking PDE-5 inhibitors such as avanafil, sildenafil, tadalafil, or vardenafil; concomitant use can cause severe hypotension, syncope, or myocardial ischemia. §7.1 states PDE-5 inhibitors potentiate the hypotensive effects of organic nitrates and notes that the time course and dose dependence of the interaction have not been studied.
source_claim_supported: Sublingual nitroglycerin is contraindicated in patients taking sildenafil or other PDE-5 inhibitors because the combination can cause severe hypotension, syncope, or myocardial ischemia.
blueprint_locator: Printed p. 38, Pharmacological and Parenteral Therapies: evaluate appropriateness and accuracy of medication orders; review contraindications and potential interactions before medication administration; educate clients about medications; handle and administer high-risk medications safely.
candidate_reasons_resolved: Rewrote all four alternatives as parallel medication-interaction teaching statements and removed isolated all/only wording.
Balanced option lengths so the correct answer is not conspicuously longer than the distractors.
Removed the unsupported universal one-hour separation rule and kept the item on the exact labeled contraindication.
audit_note: Independent adversarial review confirms A uniquely matches §§4.1 and 7.1. B and C invent ways to neutralize a contraindicated interaction, and D reverses the pharmacodynamic effect. No second defensible answer, unsupported interval, or material cueing remains.
